text:
alex: FYI I'm seeing a ~15% tail latency regression after the night deploy (canary group only). Flame graph shows host CPU hot on parsing/tokenization and grpc writev spikes. attaching snapshot: https://perf.internal/runs/7990009 :grimacing:

maria: ugh. which endpoints? small tokens or long context?

alex: mostly chat-streaming paths. high-percentile tails on requests >512 tokens. quick top from perf `perf top -p <pid>`:
```
20.3% host::parse_request
14.8% tokenizer::tokenize
12.1% grpc::WriteV
9.7% kernel_selector::choose_kernel_slow_path
6.4% kvcache::evict_if_needed
5.9% http2::frame_serialize
```

noah: kernel_selector slow path? did selector start choosing different kernels after the last kernel metadata bump?

alex: yeah, looks like for seq_len > 1024 the selector now prefers a "compat" kernel that avoids quant paths. throughput is lower and it amplifies when batches include many long requests. batching heuristics are coalescing long+short into one large batch.

kira: metrics show kvcache.hit_rate dipped from 98% -> 86% around the same time. eviction rate spiked (see graph): https://telemetry/kvcache/host/7990009. Could be TTL change or different prefix keys from the tokenizer output.

maria: tokenizer output changed recently? we landed that emoji-normalize PR yesterday. maybe tokenization differences change cache keys.

alex: good call — I compared tokenizer hashes and noticed extra normalization for certain unicode sequences, which changes prefix keys. That explains kvcache churn. Combined with larger batches and kernel fallback we get more CPU work per token.

noah: short term mitigations:
- add a cap: max_batch_size=8 for requests with seq>512 (force split batches)
- revert the emoji-normalize on the hot path or make it cache-stable (preserve old hashing for prefixes)
- log kernel selection reasons (why compat chosen) at debug level

alex: I can push canary for batch cap and debug logging now. should reduce the kernel fallback amplification.

maria: I'll open a revert PR for the tokenizer change and a followup that makes normalization idempotent wrt kvcache keying.

kira: I'll investigate kvcache policy: TTLs, eviction schedule, and if we can bump the hot-key allocation to avoid cross-shard evictions. Also will add a metric for "tokenizer_key_version" so we can correlate.

bench-bot: quick numbers from local bench (master vs canary):
```
master: p95=120ms p99=210ms qps=450
canary: p95=140ms p99=255ms qps=430
with batch_cap=8: p95=125ms p99=220ms qps=440
```

noah: sounds promising. longer-term: tweak kernel_selector scoring so it prefers quantized kernels if batch composition is mostly short requests, or have an adaptive split that isolates long sequences into a separate worker to avoid penalizing other traffic.

alex: agree. add to roadmap: "kernel selector: batch-aware policy" and "kvcache-stable-keying for tokenizer changes". I'll create the tickets.

maria: can we also add lightweight sampling to capture batch composition (list of seq_lens) for each kernel invocation? will help debug future regressions.

alex: yes — I'll add sampling + debug logs. noah, kira — can you both review the canary batch-cap PR when I post? aiming to roll within the hour. :thumbsup:

noah: will review quickly. if bench-bot confirms no throughput regression, approve.

kira: monitoring alert rule: spike in kvcache.evictions > 5/min triggers page. I'll tune thresholds after this incident.

alex: rolling canary now. will post updates. thanks all.

sre-bot: deploy canary started (deploy/799001). will post status.

bench-bot: ab test scheduled for 15m. will report p95/p99.

alex: update — initial canary shows p99 down ~20ms. keeping watch. planning follow-ups: ticket for kernel selector, tokenizer-keying, kvcache policy. closing loop here for now. :)
